newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH C.BANK SAYS POLICY HOLDS DESPITE CPI JUMP.
newsitem.headline: CZECH C.BANK SAYS POLICY HOLDS DESPITE CPI JUMP.

text.p: A sharp jump in Czech July consumer inflation will not force the Czech central bank (CNB) to change its interest rate policy, the Czech news agency CTK reported on Friday.

CTK quoted CNB board member Jiri Pospisil as saying July's 3.5-percent inflation rise was slightly higher than the bank's forecast for 3.2 percent, but policy would not change since the rise a result of price deregulation.
"We think that the influence is one time and will not have a further influence on the development of prices," the agency quoted him as saying.
"The same as in the past, our approach is the same, in the direction of lowering rates with care not to increase inflationary pressure," Pospisil said.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) released CPI figures on Friday showing month-on-month inflation for July was 3.5 percent -- the biggest rise since 1993 -- putting the year-on-year rate at 9.4 percent.
July's year-on-year rate is the highest since August 1996, when inflation reached 9.6 percent.

The CSU said liberalisation of rents and energy prices was at the heart of the increase, accounting for 3.252 percent points of the month-on-month figure. Core inflation for July was 0.366 percent, the bureau said.
The central bank was forced to sharply increase interest rates in late may after the crown currency came under heavy pressure from foreign hedge fund short-selling.
The CNB has gradually eased its policies since, allowing rates to fall back to levels slightly higher than in mid-May before the crisis.

On June 27 the CNB lowered its last resort lending facility for banks, the Lombard rate, to 23 percent from a previous 50 percent. Its discount rate remains unchanged from May 27, when it was raised by 250 basis points to 13 percent.
On Friday, the Prague Interbank Offered Rate (PRIBOR) for overnight funds stood at 14.43 percent, while six-month money averaged 14.44 percent.
